headline_findings: Whoop closed a $575M Series G at a $10.1B valuation in March 2026, reported $1.1B annualized bookings for 2025 (+103% YoY), 2.5M+ members and cash-flow positivity - i.e., the subscription-wearable model is now a ~9x-bookings asset [verified: Whoop press center; Yahoo Finance; Crunchbase News].

Whoop pricing is $199 (One) / $239 (Peak) / $359 (Life) per year with hardware bundled; the May 2025 attempt to charge $49/$79 upgrade fees was reversed within ~48 hours after user backlash, showing hardware-refresh promises are a liability in the HaaS model [verified: whoop.com; Bloomberg 2025-05-09; TechCrunch 2025-05-11].

The FDA warning letter to Whoop is dated 14 July 2025 (not Sept 2025 as briefed), classifying Blood Pressure Insights as a device; FDA closed it out in June 2026 after labeling changes, but a class action was filed on the back of it [verified: fda.gov; secondary: STAT 2026-06-23; ArentFox Schiff].

Whoop Strength Trainer (launched 2023-04-25) computes "muscular load" from user-logged sets/reps/weights plus IMU data - it is manual/assisted logging, not automatic rep or exercise detection, leaving the gap the owner is targeting open [verified: BusinessWire; whoop.com].

Whoop hardware is China-assembled (sensor, PCBA, battery, housing) with band attachment and firmware in the US, and CBP classifies imports under HTSUS 9031.90.9195 + 9903.88.01 (Section 301) - a China-built clone inherits the same tariff exposure [verified: Federal Register 2020-12-14; CBP N339661 2024-05-09].

Oura reported >$500M revenue in 2024, guided ~$1B for 2025, raised $900M+ at $11B (Oct 2025), and has sold 5.5M rings cumulatively; it holds ~74% of a smart-ring market that grew ~77% in 2025 to ~4.4M units [secondary: CNBC 2025-10-14; TechCrunch; Counterpoint/Omdia].

In June-Sept 2025 the screenless-band segment was simultaneously validated and commoditized: Amazfit Helio Strap $99 (no sub), Garmin Index Sleep Monitor $169.99, Polar Loop $199.99 (no sub) - $99 is now the retail floor for a 24/7 HR/HRV/sleep/temp band from a brand with an app [verified: BusinessWire 2025-06-24; Garmin newsroom; Polar press release].

Fitbit 10-Ks put scaled hardware-only wearable gross margin at 43% (2017), 40% (2018) and 29.8% GAAP (2019), eroded by smartwatch mix, promotions and tariffs - the base rate for a no-subscription hardware business [verified: SEC EDGAR FY2018/FY2019 10-K].

The strength-wearable graveyard is real: Atlas Wristband (>$500K Indiegogo 2014, "ambitious but flawed", absorbed by Peloton and cancelled) and Amazon Halo (killed April 2023, data deleted, refunds) both died on accuracy/differentiation and margin, not on demand [verified: CNBC 2023-04-26; secondary: TechCrunch 2014; AppleInsider 2016; Wareable].

Garmin's automatic rep counting is blog-reported at 80-90% on isolated arm movements and poor on bench/squat/deadlift; no vendor publishes accuracy, and a 2021 peer-reviewed validation exists but was not readable here - detection on compound lifts is the unsolved, differentiating problem [secondary: Alibaba Wellness blog; verified existence: PMC8471343].

India's wearables market shrank 4.0% to 114.2M units in 2025 (smartwatches -17.6%, boAt 29.2% share, earwear ASP $17.5) while Indian rings (Ultrahuman 30.4% domestic share, INR 28,499, no subscription) are the bright spot - India is a manufacturing/export story, not a domestic-demand story for a premium band [verified: IDC 2Q25 release; secondary: IDC FY2025 via TelecomLead/FoneArena; Smartprix].

Global wrist-worn shipments grew ~10% in 2025 (Q1: 45.6M units) with IDC forecasting 156.8M smartwatches and 35.3M wristbands for 2025; no analyst breaks out screenless bands, so the addressable segment is unmeasured and small relative to the ~190M wrist-worn base [verified: IDC prAP53613925; prUS52615024].

detailed_notes:
# Competitor landscape and business-model economics (Whoop-class screenless wearables)

Method note: 20 WebSearch queries executed before the session's search budget was exhausted; both permitted WebFetch attempts (whoop.com press center, sacra.com) were egress-blocked. Everything below is from search-result snippets. Items the brief asked for that could not be searched are listed as "not found" and in open_questions. Dates are given for every figure.

## 1. Whoop: the reference model

**Scale and capital (verified, Whoop press center / Yahoo Finance / Crunchbase News, March 2026).** Series G of $575M at a $10.1B post-money valuation, led by Collaborative Fund with 2PointZero, QIA, Mubadala, Abbott and Mayo Clinic plus athlete investors; total raised ~$979M (secondary). Whoop reported $1.1B in annualized bookings for 2025 (+103% YoY), 2.5M+ members, and said it was cash-flow positive in 2025. Derived: EV/bookings ~9.2x; bookings/member ~$440/yr, which is above the top list price and therefore signals multi-year prepay in bookings, add-ons, or member-count lag - a reconciliation item, not a fact.

**Pricing (verified, whoop.com membership pages, 2025-2026).** WHOOP One $199/yr (5.0 hardware included), Peak $239/yr, Life $359/yr (MG hardware with ECG and Blood Pressure Insights). The 4.0-era "$30/month" price in the brief was not independently verified; a blog-grade source gives "$20-30/month with steep discounts for 12- and 24-month plans".

**The May 2025 upgrade-fee backlash (verified, Bloomberg 2025-05-09, TechCrunch 2025-05-11, TechRadar).** With the 5.0/MG launch Whoop told existing members to either extend 12 months or pay a one-time $49 (5.0) / $79 (MG) upgrade fee, contradicting a since-deleted blog promise of free next-gen hardware after 6+ months of membership. Within ~48 hours it reversed: >12 months remaining = free upgrade, <12 months = extend, fees refunded. Lesson for a hardware-as-a-service model: forward promises about hardware refresh become balance-sheet liabilities and reputational convexity.

**Regulatory (verified, fda.gov).** FDA warning letter dated 14 July 2025 (MARCS-CMS 709755) - not September as the brief stated - held that Blood Pressure Insights is a medical device because target ranges and sleep-related claims imply diagnosis of hypo/hypertension; Whoop argued it is a wellness feature. STAT and MobiHealthNews report an FDA closeout in June 2026 after Whoop modified the product and labeling (secondary). A plaintiff class action citing the letter was announced in December 2025 (secondary). Read-through: any "medical-grade" language on a new device is a free option written to regulators and plaintiffs; the wellness lane (readiness, recovery, strain) is the safe lane, which happens to be where FitForge already sits.

**Strength Trainer (verified, BusinessWire 2023-04-25; vendor blog).** Launched April 2023 as the "first wearable to measure muscular load". Mechanism: the user logs sets/reps/weights (manual or from prebuilt routines; 200 workouts at launch, ~500 exercises by the 2026 update); accelerometer and gyroscope data are used to compute muscular load that feeds Strain. It is NOT automatic set/rep detection. This is the gap the owner's idea targets, and a new entrant (FORT, ex-Tesla engineers, Feb 2026, blog-sourced) is explicitly attacking it.

**Manufacturing and tariffs (verified, Federal Register 2020-12-14; CBP ruling N339661 2024-05-09).** CBP's country-of-origin determination: sensor, PCBA, battery and housing are assembled in China; in the US the module is attached to the fabric band and firmware is loaded. The 2024 ruling classifies Whoop Bands from China under HTSUS 9031.90.9195 with 9903.88.01 (Section 301 China list). A blog (the5krunner, Oct 2025) reports Whoop suing a Chinese rival over a $100 look-alike - IP enforcement risk for any Whoop-shaped clone. Alibaba/Global Sources list multiple Shenzhen "whoop band" ODMs (verified existence; prices not captured): the shell is a commodity.

**Retention (secondary, Fitt Insider / Baxter interview, undated).** >50% of members use the device daily at 18+ months; "retention north of 80% in core demographic" (definition unclear). Blog-grade claims of LTV:CAC ~4.5x and an 85/10/5 revenue split (memberships / accessories+apparel / B2B) come from a page whose own ARR projection (>$600M by 2026) is already stale, so discount them. Sacra's Whoop PDF (updated 2026-05-31) is the best next source and was blocked.

## 2. Oura and the ring segment

Oura: >$500M revenue in 2024; expected ~$1B in 2025; Series E of $900M+ at $11B led by Fidelity (Oct 14, 2025), up from $200M at $5.2B in Dec 2024; 5.5M cumulative rings by Sept 2025 vs 2.5M in June 2024 (i.e., ~3M rings in ~15 months); $250M revolver (Sept 2025). Sacra estimates $764M revenue through June 2026 (all secondary: CNBC, TechCrunch, Fierce). Derived EV/revenue ~11x vs Whoop ~9x on bookings. The $5.99/mo subscription and $349 Ring 4 price in the brief were not verified this session.

Ring market (secondary, Counterpoint/Omdia): shipments +77% YoY in 2025 to ~4.4M units, North America ~60%; H1 2025 share Oura 74%, Ultrahuman 9%, Samsung 9%, RingConn 5%. India: Ultrahuman 30.4%, Gabit 18.3% (attribution ambiguous). Ultrahuman Ring AIR lists at INR 28,499 with no subscription (vendor page verified; price is a 2026 listing). The Oura-vs-Ultrahuman/RingConn ITC patent matter could not be searched - open item with large implications for any Indian ring/band exporter to the US.

## 3. 2025: the screenless-band segment was validated and commoditized in the same quarter

Verified launches: Amazfit Helio Strap, $99, no subscription, 24 June 2025 (BusinessWire); Garmin Index Sleep Monitor, $169.99, upper-arm, sleep-only, 18 June 2025 (Garmin newsroom); Polar Loop, $199.99 / GBP 149.50, no subscription, announced 3-4 Sept 2025, shipping 10 Sept (Polar press release, Forbes). Helio Strap 2 followed in mid-2026 (blog). Price ladder: $99 < $169.99 < $199.99 = Whoop One's annual fee. Over two years Whoop One costs 2x a Polar Loop and 4x a Helio Strap - and Amazfit, Garmin and Polar bring existing apps, retail and service organizations at near-zero incremental platform cost. For a new entrant this sets the retail anchor at $99-$199 with no subscription attached, which means hardware gross profit per unit is small in absolute dollars: the value has to be in software/data, and the sensor hardware should be treated as a distribution cost for the software.

## 4. Base rates from the graveyard and from public filings

Fitbit (verified, SEC 10-Ks): gross margin 43% (2017) -> 40% (2018, smartwatch mix) -> 29.8% GAAP / 31.2% non-GAAP (2019: mix, promotions, tariffs, no warranty-accrual release). That is the scaled, hardware-only base rate, with tariffs and promotions as the drift. Amazon Halo (verified, CNBC 2023-04-26): launched 2020, killed April 2023, service off 31 July 2023, all health data deleted, refunds paid; cited reasons were a crowded segment, cost cuts and privacy blowback. Atlas Wristband (secondary): >$500K Indiegogo (2014), shipped 2015, reviewed as "ambitious but flawed" (2016), acquired by Peloton, next product cancelled with refunds - the closest analogue to the owner's idea, and it died on accuracy and scale. Pebble's Kickstarters ($10.3M 2012, $20.3M 2015, $12.8M 2016) show crowdfunding can validate demand but did not save the company (sale to Fitbit, Dec 2016, not captured in snippets). Jawbone, Misfit, Basis, Moov, Push, Beast, Peloton Guide: not searched (budget); should be filled by another lens or a follow-up.

Strength auto-tracking state of the art: Garmin auto-rep is blog-reported at 80-90% on isolated arm movements and poor on bench/squat/deadlift; a 2021 peer-reviewed validation of a smartwatch workout-analysis app (PMC8471343) exists but was not read. Apple Watch/Hevy/Gymatic, Samsung and Fitbit rep detection, and the VBT encoder pricing (Vitruve/RepOne/Tendo/GymAware/Enode) were not searched.

## 5. Market size context (IDC, verified press releases)

Global wrist-worn Q1 2025: 45.6M units (+10.5%), smartwatches 34.8M; +10% YoY through Q3 2025 (secondary). IDC forecast: smartwatches 156.8M (2025) / 159.7M (2026); wristbands 35.3M (2025) / 34.6M (2026); total wearables +3.9% in 2025. No analyst breaks out "screenless bands" as a category in any snippet seen. India (IDC): 2Q25 27M units (-9%); FY2025 114.2M units (-4.0%, second straight decline), smartwatches -17.6%, boAt 29.2% unit share, Noise leads smartwatches at 26.6%, earwear ASP $17.5. India's domestic wrist-wearable market is shrinking and ultra-low-ASP; the Indian angle is export manufacturing (Ultrahuman as proof of a premium India-built wearable) rather than domestic demand.

## 6. Distribution

Verified/secondary evidence: Amazon listings for Polar Loop; DTC vendor pages for Whoop/Polar/Amazfit/Ultrahuman; Kickstarter/Indiegogo history (Pebble, Oura, Atlas). Gym/coach B2B (Whoop Unite), Amazon fee economics, App Store commission tiers and DTC CAC benchmarks: not searched; the only CAC-type figure seen (LTV:CAC 4.5x) is blog-grade.

## 7. Trader framing: relative value, convexity, downside

- **Relative value.** Whoop ~9x bookings and Oura ~11x revenue are late-stage private marks that price in a subscription/annuity narrative; Fitbit's 30-43% hardware GM history is what a no-subscription hardware business is actually worth operationally. The market is paying for recurring revenue and data, not for bands.
- **Where the segment's price discovery landed.** $99 (Amazfit) is the 2025 clearing price for a screenless 24/7 HR/HRV/sleep/temp band from a brand with an app; $169.99-$199.99 is the premium no-sub tier; $199-$359/yr is the subscription tier. A generic tracker from a new brand cannot price above the $99-$199 band without a feature nobody else has.
- **The option.** None of the $99-$359 devices does automatic set/rep/exercise detection; Whoop's Strength Trainer is user-logged; Garmin's auto-rep is unreliable on compound lifts. If FitForge's algorithm works on compound barbell lifts, the payoff is asymmetric because it turns a commodity band into a data pipe for an existing training app with a readiness engine. If it does not, the product is a $99 commodity with a subscale supply chain - i.e., Atlas.
- **Cheapest way to buy the option.** The verified facts suggest sequencing: (1) prove the detection algorithm on IMU data from an existing device before tooling anything - Helio Strap/Polar Loop-class hardware already exists at $99-$199, and Shenzhen ODMs sell white-label shells; (2) only build custom hardware if raw IMU access from existing devices is impossible (open question) and the algorithm is demonstrably accurate.
- **Downside drivers.** Incumbents' zero-marginal-cost entry (Amazfit/Garmin/Polar/FORT), Section 301-style tariff exposure for China-assembled units (Whoop precedent), design-IP enforcement (Whoop v. Chinese clone), regulatory drift if any medical claim is made (Whoop FDA letter), and hardware-refresh promises (Whoop upgrade backlash). Base rate for standalone strength-tracking wearables is close to total loss (Atlas, Halo).
- **Upside drivers.** Category growth (rings +77%, wrist-worn +10%), proven willingness to pay $199-$359/yr for recovery data (2.5M Whoop members, 5.5M Oura rings), and India as a credible premium-wearable origin (Ultrahuman). Nobody has yet combined auto strength logging with a Whoop-class recovery band at a no-subscription price.
